securityImpact: A standalone MCP App SDK deployment creates a new public service, identity, browser-widget, and postMessage trust boundary. Proposed ADR-012 requires Entra-issued MCP-audience tokens, connector interoperability proof, no token passthrough, delegated OBO for future API calls, strict result-channel schemas, frame/origin isolation, actor-bound sessions, least-privilege tools, sanitization, and bounded audit metadata. The ADR and exact identity configuration require human approval before implementation.
dataImpact: The proposed first slice uses synthetic server metadata only and excludes tenant, organization, property, lease, payment, maintenance, document, prompt, and model-provider data. Any business-data tool requires a separately approved task contract.
observabilityImpact: Proposed ADR-012 defines standalone health, bounded logs and metrics, correlation propagation, session and authorization signals, ownership, and alerts while excluding tokens, prompts, arguments, results, personal data, and tenant data. Implementation and retention details require Platform/SRE and Security/Privacy approval.
rollbackConsiderations: No standalone runtime or infrastructure is implemented. Before activation, rollback removes the package and Turbo wiring. After separately approved activation, containment disables connectors and ingress, revokes consent and workload access, stops the revision to invalidate ephemeral sessions, and leaves the private API and deterministic workflows unchanged.
